newsitem.title: CHINA: Earthquake rocks remote, tremor-prone China county.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks remote, tremor-prone China county.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale rocked Lijiang county in southwestern China's Yunnan province early on Wednesday, just months after a huge quake devastated the area, local officials said.

The tremor, which hit the county at around 3.25 a.m. (1925 GMT), toppled walls and sent roof tiles tumbling in the mountain villages around scenic Lijiang town, an official of the county's anti-earthquake headquarters said.
Local officials contacted by telephone said 17 people in villages near the county centre had been injured, but none seriously.
"We have sent people to investigate...we don't think there will be many casualties because this is a mountain area and the population is sparse," she said.

Lijiang county has been struggling to rebuild its economy and tourist industry since an earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale hit the area on February 3, killing at least 304 people and injuring more than 16,000.
The Xinhua news agency said Wednesday's earthquake had hit the same area as the February catastrophe.
It was followed by a landslide that hit an area 100 km (60 miles) from the county centre at dawn, the official agency said but gave no details.

Lijiang town's traditional architecture and Naxi ethnic minority population have long made it one of Yunnan province's top tourist attractions, but the picturesque area has been plagued by tremors in recent months.
The February quake damaged more than 1.17 million homes, completely destroyed 340,000, left 160,000 people without shelter and caused huge economic damage, local officials said.
Chinese experts say the country is currently going through a period of intense seismological activity that will last until the end of the century.
A total of 50 earthquakes measuring more than 5.0 on the Richter scale hit China in 1995, an increase of 18.5 percent from the year before, official figures show.
Tremors in China have killed more than 550,000 people since 1900, accounting for 53 percent of the world's total deaths from earthquakes, Xinhua said in June.
